dimensions.assessment: Affects applicants for public land rights-of-way for hyperscale data centers, the Bureau of Land Management, and local communities near proposed data centers.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall require an applicant for a right-of-way for the use, occupancy, or development of public lands for a hyperscale data center to submit, as an addendum

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory environmental impact statements, public hearings, detailed 10-year resource consumption projections, and workforce plans on data center projects.
dimensions.evidence: The issuance, amendment, modification, renewal, or revision by the Director of the Bureau of Land Management of any permit, lease, or other authorization for the use, occupancy, or development of public lands for a hyperscale data center shall be considered a major Federal action

dimensions.assessment: Requires additional staffing and administrative resources for the Bureau of Land Management to carry out expanded environmental reviews and reports.
Amends the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 and alters how the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 applies to certain data center permits.
dimensions.evidence: Section 501(b) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1761(b)) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory requirements for all future and revised right-of-way authorizations and leases for qualifying data centers on public lands.

missing_information: Specific estimates of the federal cost to implement these new reviews.
Exact number of current or future public land data center projects that would meet the 50-megawatt threshold.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes new procedural, analytical, and workforce plan requirements for hyperscale data centers on public lands, moderately affecting developers, federal land management agencies, and local communities.
